transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

A 'funny smell' from a fridge-freezer usually points to one of two very different things: either something organic has gone wrong inside the appliance itself, or there is an electrical issue. We need to be careful. First, please check for safety signs. Is there any smell of burning plastic, hot wires, or visible scorching on the plug or where the fridge sits? Does the appliance trip your RCD (fuse) when plugged in or when you hear a click/hum from the compressor trying to start? If you see scorching, smell burning, or it trips the electrics: STOP using it immediately and leave it unplugged. This indicates an electrical fault that requires a qualified engineer. If there are no electrical signs (no trip, no burn smell), the smell is likely from food residue trapped in hidden areas like the drain hole at the back of the fridge compartment or under the crisper drawers, which standard cleaning might miss. Please let me know about the electrical checks first.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Well, now you mention it, it does smell a bit like hot plastic, an electrical sort of smell, more round the back than inside. The plug feels a little warm too, and there's a buzzing from the back sometimes. No smoke though, and the fuse box hasn't tripped.

The combination of an electrical 'hot plastic' smell near the back, a warm plug, and intermittent buzzing is a clear warning sign. It suggests an electrical component—most likely the compressor start relay or overload protector—is overheating due to a fault, or there is internal wiring insulation breaking down as it heats up. This is not something to ignore. Even though it hasn't tripped the fuse yet, this level of heat can melt the plug pins or damage the socket, creating a fire risk. Please check one specific thing: listen closely to the back of the fridge over the next few minutes. Does the compressor kick in with a 'click' followed by a hum (the normal start cycle), and does the buzzing/warmth spike at that moment? Or is it just a constant low buzz? In the meantime, I strongly advise you to unplug the appliance from the wall socket now. Do not use it until an engineer has inspected the electrical connections and the compressor terminals. This is a safety-critical issue.

Spoiled food residue in hidden areas (medium)
Drain blockage causing stagnant water smell (low)

Checks they have done and what they found: cleaned it out - smell is still there.
The fault they reported is: "funny smell in the kitchen". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

The next check, chosen from the evidence: "note exactly when it trips - on plug-in, when the compressor tries to start, or after running". Give this check, and only this one, as short safe steps, with what each result would mean.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.
